Vermont Department of Taxes, Property Valuation and Review annual report data: taxes and tax rates by town (tax year 2022)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.

Public schools are run by a separate school district and funded through the statewide Education Fund. The city bills the education property tax with its own and pays it over; residents pay both, but only the city's own share is counted here.

The city reported $8,982,000 of property tax, which includes $4,578,010 of education property tax billed for the school district (the Vermont Department of Taxes lists $5,095,648 of education tax and $4,403,990 of municipal tax for tax year 2022). Only the city's own municipal share, $4,403,990, is counted.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: the Secretary of State's campaign finance system refused connections from the build environment, and most town candidates do not file there.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
